items.prompt: White to move. Each side has already played one pawn move (h3 and ...h6). The record is just e4: a square name with no letter in front, so a pawn moves there. Play it.

claims.statement: The pawn on e2 can go to e4.
A white pawn stands on e2.

hints: A record with no capital letter is a pawn move.
The record names only the landing square, e4. Which pawn can get there?
The pawn on e2 advances two squares to e4.
items.explain: No letter means a pawn, and e4 is where it lands. The pawn on e2 is the one that can get there, so e4 is a complete record.

items.prompt: White to move. Each side has already played one pawn move (h3 and ...h6). The record says Nc3. N is the knight and c3 is its landing square. Tap the square where the knight lands.

claims.statement: The knight on b1 can go to c3.
A white knight stands on b1.

hints: The last two characters of a record are the landing square.
N says which kind of piece moves; c3 says where it lands.
items.explain: The capital letter names the piece and the last two characters name the landing square, so Nc3 sends a knight to c3.

items.prompt: White to move. The record says Bc4. B is the bishop. Play that move.

claims.statement: The bishop on f1 can go to c4.
A white bishop stands on f1.

hints: B is the bishop. Which of your bishops can move now?
The bishop slides along a diagonal to c4.
The bishop on f1 goes to c4.
items.explain: B is the bishop and c4 is where it lands. Only the bishop on f1 can get there, so Bc4 names one move.

items.prompt: White to move. The record says Qh5+. Q is the queen, h5 is the landing square, and + means the move gives check. Play it.

claims.statement: The queen on d1 can go to h5.
After Qh5 the queen attacks the king on e8, so it is check.

hints: The + at the end tells you the move gives check.
The queen slides along the diagonal that starts at d1.
The queen goes from d1 to h5 and attacks the king on e8.
items.explain: The queen slides up the diagonal to h5. Black's f-pawn has left f7, so the diagonal to the king is open and the queen attacks it. The + reports that.

items.prompt: White's king is about to go to c1 and the rook to d1, castling toward the a-file. Which record is this?

claims.statement: The king can castle to c1.
Castling to g1 is not possible, because the knight is still on g1.

hints: Castling toward the a-file is the long way round.
Castling the short way needs f1 and g1 empty. Is g1 empty here?
The king goes to c1, the long way, written with three O's.
items.explain: The king goes to c1 and the rook to d1, toward the a-file. That is the long way, written O-O-O. The short way is not even possible here.

items.prompt: White to move. The record says a8=Q: the pawn lands on a8 and becomes a queen. Play it and pick the queen.

claims.statement: The pawn on a7 can promote to a queen on a8.
A white pawn stands on a7.

hints: The pawn is one step from the last rank.
The record gives the landing square, then = and the new piece.
Move the pawn from a7 to a8 and choose a queen.
items.explain: The pawn reaches the last rank on a8 and the =Q names what it becomes. The same pawn could become a rook, a bishop or a knight instead.
